identity.summary: A conceptual introduction to the Internet of Things, drawn from the Getting Started module of Microsoft's open-source "IoT for Beginners" curriculum: what IoT is, the parts of an IoT device, how sensors and actuators let a device interact with the physical world, and how devices connect to and communicate over the internet.

brief.audience: Developers, students, and technology professionals new to IoT, with basic programming familiarity assumed
brief.intended_learning_outcome: Explain what the Internet of Things is, describe the parts of an IoT system (devices, sensors, actuators, and connectivity), and outline how IoT devices connect to and communicate over the internet

sources.title: IoT for Beginners - Introduction to IoT

access.basis: Public MIT-licensed Microsoft curriculum on GitHub

sources.activity_purpose: Understand what IoT is, see everyday examples, and learn the high-level anatomy of an IoT application.

sources.title: IoT for Beginners - A deeper dive into IoT

access.basis: Public MIT-licensed Microsoft curriculum on GitHub

sources.activity_purpose: Learn the components of an IoT device, how microcontrollers and single-board computers differ, and how they run code.

sources.title: IoT for Beginners - Interact with the physical world with sensors and actuators

access.basis: Public MIT-licensed Microsoft curriculum on GitHub

sources.activity_purpose: Understand what sensors and actuators are, the difference between analog and digital, and how a device reads and acts on the world.

sources.title: IoT for Beginners - Connect your device to the Internet
sources.activity_name: Connect a device to the internet

access.basis: Public MIT-licensed Microsoft curriculum on GitHub

sources.activity_purpose: See how IoT devices communicate using MQTT and publish/subscribe messaging to and from the cloud.
